comparison: Strong agreement on predictive accuracy claims (C2, C3, C42-C45, C41). Both evaluations affirm the high performance metrics and validation approach. OpenEval provides more technical detail about correlation (r=0.99) and blinding methodology, while peer reviewers use terms like 'compelling' and 'proof-of-principle evidence.'

Complete agreement on mechanistic findings (C4, C39-C40, C70-C71). Both evaluations support the conclusion that PKP2 patients show genotype-specific EP remodeling beyond structural factors. Peer reviewers explicitly endorsed the interplay between structure and electrophysiology, matching OpenEval's interpretation of correlation data.

Strong agreement on PKP2 cell model development (C20-C27, C48-C50, C84-C85). Both evaluations praise the genotype-specific modeling approach. OpenEval notes lack of independent validation, while peer reviewers call it 'innovative' without raising validation concerns. Peer R3 also includes calcium handling claims (C51-C52) that OpenEval addresses separately in R11.

Agreement on restitution analysis (C28-C29, C65-C69). Both evaluations accept the electrophysiological findings as mechanistically sound. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of restitution properties, while peer reviewers accept these as part of broader mechanistic insights. OpenEval R5 also addresses C115-C117 which peer R4 includes.

Agreement on mechanistic explanation of reduced Vmax and conduction velocity (C46-C47, C115-C117). Peer reviewers endorsed mechanistic insights broadly, while OpenEval provides detailed assessment of computational observations and restitution analysis. Both support the link between cellular properties and VT mechanisms.

Agreement on structural analysis findings (C30-C33). Both evaluations support the quantitative structural measurements. Peer R5 also addresses genotype-specific distribution differences (C34-C37, C110-C112) that OpenEval covers separately in R7, but both accept the finding of structural differences between genotypes.

Agreement on genotype-specific structural differences (C34-C37, C110-C112). Both evaluations support the finding that different genotypes exhibit distinct distributions. OpenEval notes small sample size and deviation from literature expectations, while peer reviewers emphasize the ability to distinguish electrical and morphological profiles between genotypes.

Agreement on patient characteristics and sample size (C12-C19, C56). Both evaluations accept the small sample size as appropriate given disease rarity. OpenEval notes potential generalizability concerns (high female proportion), while peer reviewers frame small sample size as reflecting modeling requirements rather than a study flaw.

Perfect claim overlap (C72-C74, C78) but different evaluation types. OpenEval rates these future application claims as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative and require prospective validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED but appropriately treat as future applications requiring further studies. Both recognize these are not demonstrated results but potential applications.

Agreement on limitation regarding genotype coverage (C106-C107). Both evaluations accept this limitation as reasonable. OpenEval also addresses small sample size and RV focus (C56-C57) which peer reviewers discuss separately. Both view the two-genotype limitation as justified by data availability.

Agreement on simulation methodology (C38, C101-C105). Both evaluations accept the comprehensive pacing protocol and blinding approach. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of methodology, while peer reviewers accept it without specific concerns as part of the overall validated approach.

Agreement on image processing and reconstruction methods (C53-C54, C96-C99). Both evaluations support the methodology. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of specific technical parameters, while peer reviewers praise the comprehensive methodology as 'exemplar in the field.' Peer R8 covers broader methodological scope including claims OpenEval addresses in R10, R13, and R17.

Agreement on diffuse fibrosis modeling (C90-C95). Both evaluations accept the experimental basis and parameterization. OpenEval notes this represents established approach from prior work, while peer reviewers praise the overall modeling as 'well thought out and thorough.'

Agreement on methodological framework (C58, C82-C83, C100). Both evaluations support the integration of imaging-based structure with genotype-specific cellular models. OpenEval identifies this as the novel contribution, while peer reviewers praise the personalized patient model approach as a major strength.

Agreement on calcium handling modifications (C51-C52, C86-C89). OpenEval notes these are based on experimental data with reasonable biological interpretation, though independent validation would strengthen claims. Peer reviewers accept the genotype-specific cell modeling without raising validation concerns, treating calcium handling as part of the innovative modeling approach.

Both address correlation between simulated and clinical VTs (C41). OpenEval emphasizes this validates the Geno-DT approach with excellent agreement (r=0.99), while peer reviewers cite this as evidence of predictive accuracy. Both treat this as strong validation of the computational approach.

OpenEval evaluated background/contextual claims (C1, C6-C11, C59-C64) as appropriately cited from established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on novel findings and methodology rather than background claims.

OpenEval evaluated additional contextual claims (C75-C76, C108-C109, C114) providing study rationale as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these represent justification rather than findings requiring peer assessment.
